summary: Specifies how to use the DES encryption algorithm in output feedback mode with the Telnet encryption option. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This picks the older DES scrambler, run in a different way, for hiding Telnet text.

questions: how does des ofb work with telnet
subtitle: Encrypting Telnet sessions using DES in a streaming mode.

tldr.problem: Telnet transmits everything in plain text, so passwords and commands are visible to anyone watching the network.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2953 specifies how to use the DES encryption algorithm in output feedback mode to encrypt Telnet traffic, using random initial vectors and key negotiation.
tldr.outcome: Telnet sessions can be encrypted with DES, though output feedback mode does not guarantee data integrity, so an attacker can still modify text if they can predict the plaintext.

today: RFC 2953 is Informational and has not been obsoleted. DES is now considered weak by modern standards, and Telnet itself is rarely used today due to SSH providing both encryption and authentication.

sections.title: DES Encryption for Telnet
sections.content:
RFC 2953 specifies how to use the Data Encryption Standard (DES) algorithm in output feedback mode with Telnet's encryption option. Output feedback mode encrypts a stream of data by generating a sequence of key material from DES and combining it with the plaintext using exclusive-or.

The two sides of a Telnet connection negotiate an initial 8-byte vector and confirm its receipt before starting encryption. Once negotiated, they exchange key identifiers to select which shared key to use, then begin encrypting data.
sections.eli5: Before scrambling, the two computers agree on a starting number, then turn on DES scrambling to hide their messages.

sections.title: Initial Vector and Key Negotiation
sections.content:
The encryption process begins when one side sends an 8-byte initial vector in a plain Telnet command. The other side responds with acceptance or rejection. Once accepted, they negotiate a key identifier (keyid) value that selects a shared encryption key, derived from Telnet's authentication mechanism or administrator configuration.

The DES algorithm is initialized with the initial vector, then produces a stream of output blocks. Each block is combined with 8 bytes of plaintext using exclusive-or to produce 8 bytes of ciphertext. If encryption is turned off and back on with the same keyid, the state must be preserved to maintain correct decryption.
sections.eli5: The starting number and key choice are sent before encryption begins, so both sides know how to scramble and unscramble.

sections.title: Security Properties and Limitations
sections.content:
Output feedback mode provides confidentiality but not integrity. If an attacker can predict the plaintext that is being sent, they can modify any byte of the ciphertext without detection. For this reason, Cipher Feedback mode, which detects some modifications, is preferred when available.

The RFC notes that adding a message authentication code (MAC) would provide integrity but would significantly increase overhead, particularly harmful on slow dialup links common at the time. DES key size (56 bits) was also a concern, though the RFC leaves key strength to the authentication option to determine.
sections.eli5: DES scrambling keeps messages secret, but it cannot stop someone from changing the scrambled text. A message authentication code would help but would make messages much bigger.
